rubric_notes: No evidence bundle. Family codes swapped (TAFs given as a.22.1.2, archaeal as a.22.1.3). Invents a separate NC2/Dr1-DRAP1 family (actually in a.22.1.3) and omits the bacterial histone-fold family a.22.1.4 (must_include). Places HU/IHF in class d superfamily 'd.12.1 Bacterial histone-like protein' (SCOPe: a.55.1). Asserts variants H2A.Z/H3.3/CENP-A as curated a.22.1.1 members without support. Homology-vs-function caveats and single-superfamily reasoning are sound and it hedges on later additions, but wrong relationship-bearing family classifications cap bio at 2 and fabricated placements cap factual at 1. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evolutionary reasoning (superfamily-level remote homology, family divergence, no substrate/pathway/quaternary transfer, external evidence list) is sound, but the family identifiers are wrong: states MazG-like is a.204.1.1 and HisE-like a.204.1.2, whereas SCOPe 2.08 has a.204.1.2 (MazG-like) and a.204.1.4 (HisE-like), with a.204.1.1 being dUTPase. No API evidence, no sunids. Wrong family classification triggers the bio <= 2 ceiling; factual support is sparse and contains a major classification error.

Correct families c.55.1.1/c.55.1.3/c.55.1.4 in c.55.1 and fold c.55; honest that identifiers are from memory. Biological reasoning is thorough: remote homology with Bork/Sander/Valencia motifs, conserved Mg-ATP site and closure mechanism, explicit unsafe transfers (substrate, regulation, oligomerisation, catalytic competence, template), fold-level no homology claim, and external evidence needed. Factual weaknesses: no API evidence for any release-specific claim, and asserts xylulokinase/fuculokinase/gluconokinase are in c.55.1.4, whereas the 2.08 Glycerol kinase family contains only the Glycerol kinase protein node (noncentral error). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Meets all must_include: families a.25.1.1/1.2/1.3 under a.25.1; divergence after duplication from an ancestral di-metal bundle rather than convergence; unsafe function/metal/EC transfer rejected; external evidence (motifs, EPR/spectroscopy, assays, phylogenetic context) listed; a.24 hemerythrin contrast correct. Factual support is correct but sparse: no evidence bundle, no sunids, no release citation. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Materially wrong relationship-bearing classification: PAD4 N-terminal domain placed in a separate superfamily b.6.2 (SCOPe: family b.6.1.6 within b.6.1; b.6.2 is SAG1) and ephrin given as b.6.1.4 (SCOPe: b.6.1.5); other PAD4 domains also misassigned (b.1.18, d.166 vs b.2.9.1, d.126.1.5). Fails must_include #1 and misstates SCOPe's homology claim for PAD4-N; hard ceiling applied. Function-transfer refusal and hierarchy semantics otherwise sound. No evidence bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Reasoning is complete: superfamily = probable common origin of a protein-interaction scaffold; forbids transferring conjugation to UBX/RBD or embedded UBLs, p97 binding to ubiquitin/RBD, GTPase binding to ubiquitin/UBX, within-RBD selectivity, fold-level relatives (MoaD/ThiS analogy), class d; lists external evidence. Factual support weak: no evidence bundle or release-specific verification; cites obsolete sid format 'd1ubq__' (SCOPe uses d1ubqa_); misassigns APG12-like to d.15.1.6 (BM-002-like) instead of d.15.1.7. Central family SCCS correct.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. No evidence bundle. Misstates families: assigns ODC wing to c.23.1.2 and KaiA N-domain to c.23.1.3 'KaiA/RbsU domain' (actual: c.23.1.4 and c.23.1.5; c.23.1.2 is ethylene-receptor receiver, c.23.1.3 is AmiR), and populates the ODC wing family with eukaryotic ODC entries (1QU4, 7ODC) although SCOPe c.23.1.4 holds only Lactobacillus 30a. Wrong relationship-bearing family classification caps biological reasoning at 2; fabricated release-specific SCCS caps factual support at 1. Functional-transfer reasoning (pseudo-receiver, non-catalytic wing, external evidence) is otherwise sound.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. No evidence bundle. Never gives the b.84.5 identifier or any sunid; omits the b.84.4 Ribosomal L27 superfamily from the siblings. Falsely states the superfamily was added around SCOP 1.73 and that SCOPe freezes manual superfamily assignments from SCOP 1.75, whereas b.84.5 is a SCOPe 2.06 manual addition absent from 1.75. Mischaracterizes the superfamily as 'essentially monotypic ... the same protein' when it contains two protein entries (V1 and A1) from three species, undermining the family-vs-superfamily discussion. Describes the bulge as an insertion in the N-terminal barrel rather than within the c.37.1.11 domain. Fold-vs-superfamily semantics and the 'not asserted, not positively convergent' caveat are stated correctly ('asserts analogy' is immediately qualified), and function/template transfer is rejected, but the required SCOPe-specific placement and supporting facts are missing or wrong.

Materially wrong classification: swaps f.21.1/f.21.2 labels and places the nitrate reductase gamma chain as a family inside the di-heme cytochrome superfamily, denying the existence of f.21.3; consequently asserts SCOPe homology between NarI and di-heme cytochromes that SCOPe does not make. Claims this holds 'SCOP 1.75 through 2.08' without any evidence. Generic fold-vs-superfamily reasoning and external-evidence list are sound, but hard ceiling for wrong relationship-bearing superfamily applies (bio<=2). No evidence bundle.

No evidence bundle; family sccs codes, superfamily and fold description are correct from knowledge. Reasoning is sound: superfamily grouping as remote homology from structure plus dinucleotide-binding mode, different families implying no clear sequence similarity, fold-level similarity to c.3/c.4 weaker and not homology, and explicit refusal to transfer activity, cofactor identity, EC number or substrate; required external evidence listed. Factual issues: asserts the RCK domain's transmembrane partner is not in SCOPe at all, which is incorrect for MthK whose pore region is classified in the membrane class; the SCOP 1.75 through 2.08 stability claim is unverified; no release or sunid support. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Misstates the classification: treats protein names 'Amyloidogenic design-1' and 'Unnamed design-1' as families and asserts the domains are in different families, when both are in family k.40.1.1 (sunid 100905). Generalizes 'not a true' annotations to fold/superfamily/family nodes; only the family carries that comment. No sccs or sunid given. Correct final conclusion via class k reasoning, but wrong relationship-bearing classification caps bio at 2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. No evidence bundle. Misstates the 1.69 state as same fold c.23 with a separate PA1492 superfamily; in fact PA1492 was its own fold c.137 (must_include 1 failed, and the summary's 'fold-level analogous relationship in 1.69' is wrong). Fabricates superfamily c.23.12 and families c.23.12.1/c.23.12.2 (actual c.23.14, c.23.14.1/c.23.14.2). Uses historical d1t1ja_ as the current SID, violating must_avoid. Only the generic direction (upgrade to superfamily-level homology, separate families, no function transfer) is correct, and the evolutionary-level definitions are sound, but the supporting classifications are wrong throughout. Wrong superfamily/family and wrong 1.69 placement cap bio at <=2; largely fabricated support gives factual 0.

Reasoning complete: tag correctly placed in class l l.1.1.1, d1a14h1 b.1.1.1 VH 9-111 identified, homology rejection well argued with level-specific caveats for real Ig matches. Empty bundle; classifications correct but unverified. Speculation that the 8 residues might be a FLAG octapeptide is hedged and flagged for confirmation but is inconsistent with the actual SEQRES (QVQLQQSG), a noncentral imprecision.

States SCOP 1.75 carved chain A into four domains d1acca1-d1acca4 with invented residue ranges and invented superfamily placements, directly violating the must_avoid item that 1.75 already had multiple domains. Never reports the actual one-domain record d1acca_ / f.11.1.1, the 2.04 split, the boundaries A:14-225 and A:226-735, or the b.179.1.1 / f.60.1.1 placements. Generic modularity and search-hygiene discussion rests on a fabricated historical premise, so reasoning is unsupported; small correct element is the identity and release dates of 1.75.

No evidence bundle. Lists Jab1/MPN (c.97.3) as one of the five domains and omits the bromodomain; boundaries invented (1-~870, 880-1300, 1300-1650, 1650-1900, 2100-2400) and no d3jb9a5/d.394 identifier. Interpretation of mosaic evolution, superfamily-level ancestry, and pseudoenzyme caveats is sound, but the material misclassification caps biological reasoning at 2.

The modular-repeat explanation of the length span and the caveats on specificity, template asymmetry and representative choice are reasonable, but the 're' heterogeneity annotation and the canonical representative repeat unit are absent, so the repeat-annotation ceiling applies. Supporting facts are unreliable: fold a.298 is named 'TAL effector' rather than the left-handed alpha-alpha superhelix, the superhelix handedness is reversed relative to the SCOPe fold description, an automated sequence-assignment workflow is asserted although these three sit under curated protein nodes, and the release in which the fold appeared is guessed. No evidence is supplied. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Pretrained-only; no evidence bundle. Correctly identifies 2.08 as stable and gives correct citation guidance (stable 2.08 vs full dated periodic label) and correct stable-vs-periodic semantics. Does not report what the current-release endpoint actually says for the latest periodic update (explicitly unverified), so the first must_include item is unmet. Honest about limits; no fabricated values; no must_avoid violations.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Pretrained, explicitly unverified. Reasoning covers must_include items in spirit (fragments retained in a.47.2.1 by homology and flagged as partial; four-helix fold supported by 1dn1 B; fragment fold assignments weaker and conformation-dependent; limits on function transfer and representatives). Factual errors: SNARE complex given as h.1.2.1 (actual h.1.15.1), 1vcs attributed to Vam3p (it is Vti1-like 2; Vam3p is 1hs7), Tlg1 listed in a.47.2.1 without support; misses 1dn1 obsolescence and 2.08 automated-match status and the explicit 'ms' annotation.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Reasoning is complete and well-hedged: level-by-level evolutionary strength, superfold argument, explicit statement that 'different fold' in SCOPe means 'no accepted evidence of homology' rather than proven independent origin, converse failure within c.2.1, and the full set of evidence SCOP-style curation requires. No evidence bundle (answer admits pretrained knowledge). Classification error: dihydrodipicolinate reductase and UDP-glucose dehydrogenase N-terminal domains are c.2.1.3 (GAPDH-like), not c.4.1. Other placements (c.3, c.31, c.66, c.1.7, c.82, c.71, d.166, c.26.2, b.35, b.47/c.41) are correct.

Reverses the central conclusion: denies any 2.04-to-current reclassification and asserts the pair is only fold/analogy level, when the ColG domain moved from b.23.2 to family b.18.1.36 inside superfamily b.18.1, which already held the Cry3A domain at b.18.1.3. Also wrongly claims the two domains share a fold in 2.04 while they did not, and declines to give any classification identifiers. Good caveat discipline on function transfer does not offset the reversed relationship. No supporting evidence supplied.

Pretrained-only answer with no evidence. Correct on hierarchy level semantics and family-level homology, but misinterprets hf as fragment/extended-construct/multi-domain heterogeneity and asserts both domains 'share the canonical three-helix bundle', the must_avoid assumption. Does not recognize hf as a different observed fold, treats the two as possibly different homeodomain subclasses although they are the same protein, and leaves identities unverified.

Biological reasoning is complete and correct: family-level homology unaffected, fragment regions treated as missing data, coverage-reported scores, complete domain preferred as representative/template, fragment retained but flagged, diversity statistics from complete domains, no function transfer, external evidence named. Factual support is essentially absent: no evidence bundle, no sunids, no domain boundaries, no fr definition, no quality fields for the recommended representative d1uc6a1; states where the annotation lives from memory (dir.des/dir.cla) and speculates the SEQRES may be truncated, which is not the case here. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Biological reasoning complete: new superfamily in existing fold; family = homolog claim licensing unsafe transfer (rejected); superfamily split = same architecture with no descent claim, convergence possible; new fold reserved for genuinely different topology. Nested-hypothesis framing, revisable with listed evidence, rejects function transfer and homology modelling across superfamilies, notes manual curation. Factual deduction: cites 'four-helical up-and-down bundle f.1 / a.24'; a.24 is correct but f.1 in SCOPe is the toxins' membrane translocation domains fold, so the f.1 identifier is misstated (noncentral example). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Mechanistic and evolutionary discussion is detailed and the substrate/regulation limits are well stated, but family identifiers are wrong: PI3K given as d.144.1.1, APH as d.144.1.2, choline kinase as d.144.1.4 (actual d.144.1.4 PI3K, d.144.1.6 APH, d.144.1.8 choline kinase). Also asserts without evidence that these assignments are stable across 2.01-2.08. No evidence bundle. Wrong family classifications trigger bio <= 2 ceiling; nonexistent release-specific sccs values give factual 1.
